findings.evidence: Mathlib `partition (σ : Perm α) : (Fintype.card α).Partition` and `exists_with_cycleType_iff {m} : (∃ g, g.cycleType = m) ↔ (m.sum ≤ Fintype.card α ∧ ∀ a ∈ m, 2 ≤ a)` are proved for `variable [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]`; the PR proof uses only `Fintype.card_fin` to pin `n`.
findings.fix: Prove the general form: `def permConjClassPartition {α} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] : ConjClasses (Equiv.Perm α) → (Fintype.card α).Partition`, `noncomputable def permEquivConjClasses ... : (Fintype.card α).Partition ≃ ConjClasses (Equiv.Perm α)`, and `Fintype.card (ConjClasses (Equiv.Perm α)) = Fintype.card (Fintype.card α).Partition`. Derive the roadmap-named `Fin n` versions as specializations via `Fintype.card_fin`.
findings.issue: Under-generalization: `card_conjClasses_perm_eq_card_partition`, `partitionEquivConjClasses`, and their supporting lemmas (`finPermPartition`, `finPermPartition_eq_iff`, `exists_perm_partition_eq`, `permConjClassPartition`, `permConjClassPartition_injective/surjective`) are stated only for `Fin n`. The theorem `ConjClasses (Equiv.Perm α) ≃ (Fintype.card α).Partition` holds for any `[Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]`, which is the natural Mathlib level — Mathlib's own `Equiv.Perm.partition`, `partition_eq_of_isConj`, and `exists_with_cycleType_iff` are all stated generally in α.

findings.evidence: `finPermPartition_parts` proves `(finPermPartition n σ).parts = σ.partition.parts` by `rfl`; the wrapper only changes the index type from `Fintype.card (Fin n)` to `n`.
findings.fix: If the conjugacy-class chain is generalized to arbitrary `α`, drop `finPermPartition` and use `Equiv.Perm.partition` directly, keeping any `Fin n` cast localized to the specialization.
findings.issue: `finPermPartition n σ` is a thin reindexing of Mathlib's `Equiv.Perm.partition σ` (same parts) through `Fintype.card (Fin n) = n`. It exists only because the file works over `Fin n` instead of a general α; in the general statement above it collapses into `Equiv.Perm.partition` itself.

summary: The Young-diagram half sits at the natural level, but the entire conjugacy-class half is specialized to `Equiv.Perm (Fin n)` when the natural Mathlib level is an arbitrary `[Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]`; every step generalizes verbatim since it rests only on `Fintype.card α` facts.
